items.title: CV processing
items.goal: A PDF or Word CV in English or Simplified Chinese becomes a structured profile in under 30 seconds, with every field showing the CV text it came from. Scanned files are rejected with a clear message, failures land in a review queue, and a recruiter's corrections survive re-processing.
prd: CV processing → Formats (decided): text-based PDF, .doc and .docx, English or Simplified Chinese; scanned files rejected with a clear message → decided
CV processing → Parsed profile (approved): name, contact, work history, education, skills with source text, languages, total years calculated from work history, link to the original file → decided
CV processing → requirement 1: recruiters can edit any parsed field and their edits are kept if the CV is processed again → proposed
CV processing → requirement 2: a file that fails to parse goes to a review queue with the reason → proposed
AI pipeline → parsing: one model call per CV; Chinese PDFs that extract poorly are sent to a model that reads PDFs directly → suggested
Non-functional requirements → Speed: a CV parsed in under 30 seconds → decided
exit: English and Simplified Chinese sample CVs parse to the approved schema with source text on every field
A scanned or image-only file is rejected with a message a recruiter understands, and no OCR is attempted
Total years of experience is computed from work history, not taken from the CV's own claim
A recruiter's correction survives re-parsing the same CV
Parsing time per CV is recorded in `ai_runs` and stays under 30 seconds on the sample set
outOfScope: Recruiter upload, email intake and the OneDrive import — real-data release
Scanned CVs and OCR — an explicit non-goal
Duplicate detection — a non-goal; resubmissions become separate candidates
Consent capture and retention — real-data release

items.title: Text-based CVs are read and scanned ones are rejected clearly
items.story: As a recruiter, I want to be told plainly when a CV cannot be read because it is a scan, so that I chase the right file instead of wondering why a candidate has no profile.
ac: Given a text-based PDF or DOCX, when it is processed, then its text is extracted on the server and stored for parsing.
Given an image-only or scanned file, when it is processed, then it is rejected with a reason a recruiter understands and no text recognition is attempted.
Given a rejected file, when I look at it later, then the reason is stored against the file rather than only logged.
prd: CV processing → Formats (decided): text-based PDF, .doc, .docx; scanned or image-only files are rejected with a clear message → decided
AI pipeline → Text extraction: PDF and .docx text is extracted on the server; legacy .doc is converted in the seed script → suggested
Non-goals → scanned or photographed CVs, no text recognition

items.title: Extract text from PDF and DOCX on the server with an image-only detector
items.what: Extract text from PDF and DOCX files in server code, and detect files that are image-only so they can be rejected rather than parsed into nonsense. Test-first: the detector's threshold is logic.
scope: `src/server/cv/extract.ts` marked `import "server-only"`, returning text plus a quality signal
Failing tests first over fictional fixtures: an English text PDF, a Simplified Chinese text PDF, a DOCX, and an image-only PDF that must be detected
The image-only rule stated as a single documented threshold, not scattered heuristics
A quality signal the Chinese PDF fallback can act on (E04-S02-T03)
exclusions: Legacy `.doc` conversion — the seed does that (E03-S04-T02)
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover English PDF, Chinese PDF, DOCX and image-only detection
The image-only threshold is defined once and asserted by a test at either side of it
The extractor cannot be imported from client code
No network call is made during unit tests

items.title: Store rejection reasons and recruiter-readable messages on cv_files
items.what: Give every rejection a stable code and a recruiter-readable message, store both against the file, and make sure nothing that failed disappears silently.
scope: A closed set of rejection reasons: image-only or scanned, unsupported type, too large, extraction produced no usable text, parse failed schema validation
A message per reason in recruiter language, held in one place so the review queue and any future upload UI read the same text
Written to `cv_files` parse status and error columns
Unit tests that every reason has a message and that the set is exhaustive
done: Every rejection path writes a stored reason code and a message; a test proves the reason set is exhaustive
A scanned file's stored message names the scan as the cause and says no text recognition is available
No rejection path leaves `cv_files` without a status

items.title: The AI fills the approved profile fields and shows its source text
items.story: As a recruiter, I want each parsed field to show me the line of the CV it came from, so that I can check the AI in seconds instead of re-reading the whole document.
ac: Given an English or Chinese CV, when it is parsed, then every approved profile field is filled or explicitly empty, and each skill carries the CV text it came from.
Given a parsed profile, when total years of experience is shown, then it was computed from the work history rather than taken from a claim in the CV.
Given a parsed field's source text, when it is compared with the CV, then the quote appears in the CV verbatim; an invented quote is rejected.
Given any parse, when it completes, then a row in `ai_runs` records the input reference, model, version, cost and duration, and the duration is under 30 seconds.
prd: CV processing → Parsed profile (approved), including skills with their source text and total years calculated from work history → decided
AI governance → requirement 1: every parsed field shows the text it was based on → proposed
AI governance → requirement 2: each AI output is stored with its input, model version and date → proposed
AI pipeline → Parsing: one model call per CV → suggested
Non-functional requirements → Speed: a CV parsed in under 30 seconds → decided

items.title: Write the CV parsing schema and prompt for English and Simplified Chinese
items.what: Write the Zod output schema for the approved profile and the first version of the parsing prompt, covering English and Simplified Chinese, with the shared rules every prompt in this app carries: evidence quoted verbatim, no invention, protected attributes never inferred, and CV text treated as data rather than instructions.
scope: `src/ai/prompts/parse-cv/` : schema, prompt v1, and fictional few-shot examples in both languages
Every field's evidence requirement stated in the schema, not just the prompt
Total years left to code, not asked of the model
Prompt-injection handling: instructions inside a CV are ignored and reported
Versioning: the prompt carries a version recorded on every run
done: The schema covers every approved profile field and requires source text where the PRD does
The prompt states the shared rules: verbatim evidence, no invention, no protected-attribute inference, CV text is data
Fictional English and Simplified Chinese examples are included and contain no real person
The prompt has a version string that the service records

items.title: Build the CV parsing service with schema validation, evidence checks and ai_runs logging
items.what: Make one model call per CV through the shared AI wrapper, validate the output against the schema, verify every evidence quote appears in the CV verbatim, compute total years from the work history, and write the profile, its skills and the run record. Test-first with a fake model.
scope: `src/server/cv/parse.ts`: extract → one call → validate → verify evidence → compute total years → persist

Failing tests first with a fake model: schema violation is rejected; an invented quote fails the evidence check; overlapping jobs produce the right total years; a CV claiming more years than its history does not override the computed value
Writes `candidate_profiles`, `candidate_skills` with source text, and an `ai_runs` row with model, version, prompt version, cost and duration
No network in unit tests
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover schema rejection, invented-quote rejection, overlapping-job total years, and the claimed-years case
Every successful parse writes a profile, its skills with source text, and one `ai_runs` row
A parse failure writes a stored rejection reason rather than throwing away the file
Unit tests make no network call

items.title: Add the Chinese PDF fallback that sends the file itself when extraction is poor
items.what: Some Simplified Chinese PDFs extract badly. When the extractor's quality signal says so, send the PDF itself to a model that reads PDFs directly instead of parsing mangled text. Keep it provider-agnostic and record which path each run took.
scope: A documented quality threshold that triggers the fallback, reusing the extractor's signal
The fallback path through the same AI wrapper, with the run recording which path was used

Failing tests first with a fake model: below the threshold uses the text path, above it uses the file path, and a provider without direct file support fails with a clear message rather than silently degrading
A cost note, since sending a file costs more than sending text
exclusions: OCR of scanned files — still rejected
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover both paths and the unsupported-provider case
Every run records which path it used, visible in `ai_runs`
The threshold is defined once and documented in the prompt folder

items.title: Record parsing time and prove the under-30-second target on the sample set
items.what: The PRD sets a hard target of under 30 seconds per CV. Record the duration of every parse in `ai_runs`, and add a check over a seeded run that reports the distribution and fails if the target is missed.
scope: Duration captured around the whole parse, not just the model call, and stored on the run
A script or test that reads `ai_runs` after a seed run and reports count, median and slowest parse
A failure when the slowest parse exceeds the target, with the offending file named
A short note on what to do when the target is missed (extraction, prompt size, or provider)
exclusions: Performance tuning itself — raise findings instead
Search performance, which belongs to E07
done: Every parse writes a duration covering extraction through persistence
The check reports the distribution over a seeded run and names the slowest file
Exceeding 30 seconds fails the check rather than printing a warning

items.title: Files that fail to parse land in a review queue
items.story: As a recruiter, I want to see which CVs could not be read and why, so that nothing quietly disappears between the file arriving and a profile existing.
ac: Given a file that fails at any stage, when I open the review queue, then it appears with the reason in plain language.
Given a queued file, when I retry it, then it is processed again and leaves the queue if it succeeds.
Given a scanned file, when it appears in the queue, then the reason says it is a scan and that no text recognition is available.
prd: CV processing → requirement 2: a file that fails to parse goes to a review queue with the reason → proposed
UI design → the review-queue screen is not in the PRD screen list; confirm before building → open

items.title: Add the review-queue query and the retry action
items.what: Expose the failed files as a queue and let a recruiter retry one. The retry is always a recruiter action; nothing retries itself.
scope: A server query listing files whose parse status is failed, with their reason, file name and when they failed
A Server Action that retries one file through the same parse path and updates its status
Failing tests first: a retry that succeeds clears the file from the queue; a retry that fails again keeps it with an updated reason and attempt count
An attempt count so a file that keeps failing is visible
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover a successful retry and a repeated failure
The queue query returns only failed files, with their reason and attempt count
No code path retries a file without a recruiter action

items.title: Build the CV review queue screen
items.what: Build the review-queue screen from `design/specs/review-queue.md`: the failed files, the reason each failed in recruiter language, and a retry button. Blocked until the product owner confirms the screen is in the MVP.
scope: A route and page rendering the queue from the server query
Per row: file name, reason, when it failed, attempt count, retry
Empty, loading and error states from the shared patterns
Playwright coverage at desktop and phone width, including the no-horizontal-overflow assertion
done: The screen matches `design/specs/review-queue.md` on review at both widths
A retry from the UI reprocesses the file and the row updates
Playwright passes at `desktop` and `phone` including the overflow assertion
The product owner's confirmation is recorded before this task is started

items.title: Recruiters correct parsed fields and their edits survive re-processing
items.story: As a recruiter, I want my corrections to a parsed profile to stick, so that fixing the same wrong job title after every re-parse is not part of my week.
ac: Given I edit a parsed field, when the CV is processed again, then my edit is still what the profile shows.
Given a field I have edited, when I look at it, then I can see both my value and what the AI originally parsed.
Given I edit a field, when the change is saved, then my typed name and the time are recorded with it.
prd: CV processing → requirement 1: recruiters can edit any parsed field and their edits are kept if the CV is processed again → proposed
Data model → candidate_profiles: recruiter edits stored separately so re-parsing never overwrites them → suggested
Users → actions are tied to a typed name → decided

items.title: Store recruiter overrides separately and merge them over parsed values
items.what: Keep the AI's parsed values and the recruiter's corrections in separate storage and define one merge rule: the recruiter's value wins, always, including after a re-parse. This is the rule the seed's re-parse path depends on, so it is strictly test-first.
scope: Override storage with the field, the value, the typed name and the timestamp
A single merge function producing the profile the app displays

Failing tests first: an override survives a re-parse; a re-parse that changes an un-overridden field updates it; clearing an override falls back to the parsed value; the merge never loses the original parsed value
No merge logic anywhere but this function
exclusions: Any automatic conflict resolution that discards a recruiter value
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover override survival, un-overridden update, clearing an override, and retention of the original parsed value
Exactly one merge function exists and every read path uses it
Each override records the typed recruiter name and the time

items.title: Add edit mode to the candidate profile with the typed-name prompt
items.what: Let a recruiter correct any parsed field on the profile, asking for their name before their first change on the device, and showing clearly which values they have changed.
scope: Edit mode on the candidate profile driven by a Server Action with Zod validation
The typed-name prompt before the first change on a device, reusing `TypedNameDialog`
Edited fields visibly distinguished from parsed ones, with the parsed value still viewable
Playwright coverage: edit a field, see it persist, and see the name prompt on first use
exclusions: Editing skills' source text — the quote belongs to the CV
done: A recruiter can edit any parsed field and the change persists through a re-parse
The name prompt appears before the first change on a device and not again afterwards
An edited field is visually distinguishable and the original parsed value is still viewable
Playwright passes at desktop and phone width

items.title: Recruiters check one candidate on a profile page
items.story: As a recruiter, I want one page that shows everything known about a candidate with the CV behind it one click away, so that I can decide whether to call them without opening four things.
ac: Given a candidate, when I open their profile, then every parsed field is shown with the CV text it came from available.
Given the original CV, when I open it, then it loads through a short-lived signed link.
Given the candidate is on jobs, when I look at their history, then I see their stage history with the names of the recruiters who moved them.
prd: UI design → Candidate profile: parsed fields with source text, edit mode, original file, stage history → decided
Security (suggested) → CV files open through short-lived signed links → suggested
AI governance → requirement 1: every parsed field shows the text it was based on → proposed

items.title: Build the candidate profile screen
items.what: Build the profile from `design/specs/candidate.md`: parsed fields with expandable source quotes, a link that opens the original CV through a signed URL, and the candidate's stage history.
scope: A Server Component page reading the merged profile, skills with source text, and stage history
`SourceQuote` on every parsed field, with `lang="zh-Hans"` for Chinese text
The original-file link fetched on demand as a signed URL, not embedded in the page HTML for long
Playwright coverage at both widths with the shared accessibility assertions
exclusions: Match scores — those belong to the job's ranked list
Contacting the candidate — the portal never contacts anyone
done: Every parsed field can show the CV text it came from, including Chinese text with the right `lang`
The original file opens through a short-lived signed URL requested on demand
Stage history shows each move with the typed recruiter name and Singapore-time dates
Playwright passes at `desktop` and `phone` with the overflow and status assertions
